title: Paralegal
description:
Paralegal

Join a supportive, forward-thinking property team handling varied conveyancing and leasing work. This full-time opportunity suits someone holding the required professional registration who enjoys client contact, managing a busy caseload and progressing their career.

If you've also worked in the following roles, we'd also like to hear from you: Conveyancing Paralegal, Property Paralegal, Residential Conveyancing Paralegal, Residential Property Paralegal, Real Estate Paralegal, Conveyancing Assistant, Property Legal Assistant, Legal Assistant

Benefits include a minimum of 33 days' holiday, the option to purchase additional leave, a generous pension scheme and structured development support.

SALARY: £33,000 - £40,000 per annum (depending on experience) + Benefits

LOCATION: Edinburgh, Scotland

JOB TYPE: Full-Time, Permanent

JOB OVERVIEW

Build your property law career in a supportive environment with varied client-facing work across conveyancing and leasing. The Paralegal will manage transactions and maintain strong client contact.

Working closely with colleagues and external parties, the Paralegal will help keep matters moving accurately and on time while contributing to a busy property team.

Structured training, ongoing professional development and supported progression give the Paralegal scope to grow while supporting clients and colleagues effectively.

As a successful candidate you will join a firm that has held Investors in People accreditation since 1997 and recently gained Gold accreditation. The firm are proud to be a friendly legal practice that genuinely cares about their staff. Many of their solicitors and support staff have been with them for over 30 years, reflecting the positive, inclusive culture they have worked hard to create

DUTIES

Your duties as the Paralegal include:
- Workload and Deadlines: Manage own workload to meet client deadlines
- Client Instructions: Deal promptly with client instructions
- Property and Leasing Transactions: Manage property and leasing transactions
- Estate Agency and ESPC Matters: Liaise with the estate agent and handle ESPC matters
- Client and Third-Party Liaison: Liaise with clients, estate agents and other third parties
- File Management: Proactively attend to file management
- Team Support: Provide support to other members of the property team

CANDIDATE REQUIREMENTS

ESSENTIAL
- Professionally accredited or registered paralegal with a recognised legal professional body, with demonstrable knowledge and experience of Scots law relevant to the role
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills
- Ability to prioritise and manage a caseload effectively
- Strong business awareness of deadlines and working under pressure
- Excellent attention to detail

DESIRABLE
- Previous relevant experience
- Experience in a similar role dealing with purchase and sale transactions, title queries across Sasine and Land Registers, and notices of potential liability

BENEFITS
- Minimum of 33 days' holiday
- Option to purchase additional leave
- Generous pension scheme
- Structured training and ongoing professional development
- Supported progression and career growth
- Friendly, inclusive working environment

HOW TO APPLY

To be considered for this job vacancy, please submit your CV to our Recruitment Team who will review your details. CV's of Job Applicants meeting this requirement will be submitted to our Client for consideration. By submitting your job application to us you are hereby giving us your express consent to submit your details to our Client for this purpose.

title: Credit Controller
description:
Credit Controller - Edinburgh

Location: Edinburgh
Salary: £30,000-£35,000
Contract: Permanent
Start Date: ASAP

We're working with a well-established business in Edinburgh who are looking to appoint an experienced Credit Controller to join their finance team.

This is a great opportunity for someone with strong credit control experience who enjoys working with customers, managing their own ledger and taking a proactive approach to cash collection.

The Role

Reporting into the Finance Manager, you'll take responsibility for managing an allocated customer ledger and ensuring outstanding debts are collected efficiently and professionally.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Managing an allocated customer ledger and monitoring outstanding balances.
- Proactively contacting customers by phone and email to recover overdue payments.
- Building strong relationships with customers and internal stakeholders.
- Investigating and resolving invoice and payment queries.
- Allocating cash and ensuring customer accounts are kept up to date.
- Monitoring aged debt and escalating potential issues where required.
- Working closely with the wider finance team to improve cash collection and reduce overdue debt.
- Preparing regular aged debt reports and providing updates on collection performance.
- Supporting with account reconciliations and other finance duties as required.
- Identifying opportunities to improve credit control processes and procedures.

About You

We're looking for someone who has:
- Previous experience in a Credit Controller or similar accounts receivable position.
- Strong communication and negotiation skills.
- Confidence speaking with customers regarding outstanding payments.
- Good attention to detail and strong organisational skills.
- The ability to manage a busy ledger and prioritise effectively.
- A proactive approach to resolving queries and collecting debt.
- Good Excel and general systems skills.
- The ability to work independently while contributing positively to a wider finance team.

This would suit an experienced Credit Controller looking for their next opportunity in Edinburgh, or someone with solid Accounts Receivable experience who is ready to take on more responsibility.

description:
European Credit Controller - FTC until May 2027

100% home based

A rapidly expanding international debt collection agency is currently looking for an experienced commercial credit professional with fluency in at least one European language and English. To join its credit management team to work on a high value and complex project until May 2027.
- Part of a highly experienced and skilled global collections team
- Responsible for your own portfolio of 200+ customers accounts across a range of different industries with debt in excess of 4million
- Focusing on maximising cash collection and working towards targets
- Prior experience of working with Oracle is also highly advantageous
- Chasing high value and complex old debt (150+ days)
- Managing complex queries and disputes through to resolution
- Ensuring all updates are logged in a timely manner on system
- Adhering to country specific legal and financial regulations
- Proactively alert management to any potential compliance issues

Skills Required:
- Proven experience within commercial debt collection/credit control is essential
- Fluency in at least one European language alongside English is essential (French, Italian, Spanish, German, Dutch, Turkish, Portuguese, Greek, Bulgarian, Slovak, Slovenian, Hungarian)
- Experience of working on ERP's such as Oracle & SAP advantageous
- Excellent communication skills, strong at negotiation and dispute resolution
- Proven ability to work in a target driven environment
- Excellent time management skills
- Ability to work of own initiative
- Self motivated, with the ability to multitask and prioritise

If you are interested in this vacancy please contact Sarah Chandler at CWC Recruitment Ltd.

title: Finance Assistant
description:
Finance Assistant

Location: Edinburgh
Hours: Full-Time 35 hours per week

The Opportunity

Our client is seeking an experienced Finance Assistant to join their established finance team in Edinburgh. This is an excellent opportunity for an organised finance professional to play a key role within a diverse and growing organisation operating across multiple sectors.

Working closely with the Finance Manager, the successful candidate will support a broad range of finance and bookkeeping activities whilst helping to ensure the smooth running of the finance function.

Key Responsibilities
- Processing supplier invoices using Sage 200
- Assisting with month-end accounting processes
- Bank and credit card reconciliations

- Allocating customer and supplier payments

You'll be an experienced finance professional who enjoys working in a varied role and can manage multiple priorities effectively.

Essential Requirements
- Minimum 5 year's experience within a finance, accounts or bookkeeping role
- Previous Sage 200 experience
- Strong Microsoft Excel skills
- Experience using accounting software
- Payroll experience
- Excellent attention to detail
- Strong organisational and problem-solving skills

Benefits

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Finance Assistant looking to join a supportive and stable organisation where they can make a meaningful contribution to the wider business.

title: Company Secretary
description:
Company Secretary - Edinburgh

An excellent opportunity has arisen for a Company Secretary to join a well-established and highly regarded professional services firm. Based in Edinburgh, this role sits within a collaborative Business Law team, offering exposure to a broad client base including private individuals, entrepreneurs and family businesses.

- High attention to detail and ability to work independently
- Team-oriented with a proactive approach

Hybrid working

title: Residential Conveyancing Paralegal
description:
Residential Conveyancing Paralegal
- Annual Salary: Competitive (with annual review and potential bonus)
- Location: North Berwick
- Job Type: Full-time

We are recruiting on behalf of a prestigious law firm known for its expert legal, property, and financial services. They are seeking a Residential Conveyancing Paralegal to strengthen the team based in North Berwick. This role is ideal for someone who is dedicated to providing the highest level of advice and service to clients, and perhaps someone who is currently commuting into Edinburgh and looking for a role which is closer to home.

Day-to-day of the role:
- Act for clients purchasing new homes from housebuilders and handle the sale of their current properties where applicable.
- Take client instructions promptly to ensure progression of missives within required timescales.
- Attend meetings, taking notes as required.
- Maintain up-to-date client files with all correspondence and documents saved appropriately.
- Maintain regular contact with housebuilders' agents, sending weekly reports to ensure all parties are updated on progress.
- Draft legal documentation, including reporting on title to clients.
- Handle all aspects of the conveyancing process in purchases, sales, and, where applicable, re-mortgages.
- Manage post-settlement work, with the support of a Conveyancing Assistant.

Required Skills & Qualifications:
- Proven experience as a Paralegal within Residential Conveyancing.
- Strong understanding of the conveyancing process.
- Excellent organisational and time management skills.
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
- Strong communication skills and attention to detail.
- Commitment to maintaining high standards of client service.

Benefits:
- Competitive salary with annual review and potential bonus based on performance.
- 32 days holiday per year, including Bank Holidays.
- Birthday off.
- 3x Death in Service Benefits.
- Hybrid Working options.
- Membership of an occupational pension scheme.
- Wellbeing initiatives and access to an online Health Provider.

To apply for this Residential Conveyancing Paralegal position, please submit your CV or reach out to Kate Irvine at Reed for more information.

title: Logistics Coordinator
description:
Our client are a leading manufacturer of precision parts for the aerospace industry. They are looking to add a Logistics Coordinator to their team on a permanent basis. This would be a great fit for a meticulous individual who enjoys challenge and variety in their day to day.

Logistics Coordinator
Permanent position
Global manufacturer of precision components
10% matched pension, 25 days holiday & life assurance

Overall Responsibilities of the Position
- Co-ordinate day to day freight, shipping and transport operations.
- Collate and maintain production, inspection and test information.
- Co-ordinate test rings and accurately record and input results.
- Prepare, check and control all shipping and export documentation.
- Ensure compliance with relevant export control and customs requirements.
- Support weekend working at month end and undertake overtime requirement to support operational requirements.
- Preparation of Metallographic samples following successful completion of training.

Key Area Responsibilities
- Liaise with shipping and transport providers to co-ordinate the movement of products by road, rail, sea and air.
- Organise miscellaneous transport services to support operational and business requirements.
- Work closely with shipping companies to maximise the efficient use of container and vehicle capacity whilst managing transportation costs effectively.
- Prepare and maintain all required certification, shipping, and export documentation, ensuring accuracy and compliance.
- Maintain accurate finished product records using Infoflo and other relevant business systems.
- Ensure records and information are accurate, up to date, secure and readily retrievable.
- Identify and support opportunities for continuous improvements.
- Liaise effectively with sub-contractors and intra-company process personnel to co-ordinate activities and resolve operational requirements.
- Participate in customer inspection and documentation reviews
- Assist with monitoring expenditure against shipping budget and identify opportunities to improve cost efficiency.
- Represent the shipping team at production, planning and other meetings providing updates as required.

Knowledge and Experience
- Good understanding of the overall product process is preferred.
- Excellent attention to detail with a high level of accuracy
- Strong IT skills to include Microsoft Office
- Previous experience of ERP systems
- Ability to understand and work to budgetary constraints
- Strong numerical and analytical skills.
- Excellent communication skills, with confidence to liaise effectively with external agencies, freight providers, subcontractors and internal stakeholders.
- Experience of quality auditing is desirable
- Previous export compliance experience desirable
- Ability to use initiatives and respond effectively to changes, issues or deviations from planned activities.
- Strong organisation and time-management skills with the ability to prioritise competing demands and meet tight deadlines.
- Comfortable communicating and working effectively with colleagues and stakeholders at all levels within the organisation.

Working Hours:
Monday - Thursday 8am - 4:15pm
Friday 8am - 3:15pm

Benefits
- 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays
- 10% matched pension
- 3x annual salary life assurance
- Profit related bonus scheme

This position is subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) which requires the jobholder to obtain certain authorisation or security clearances that will require interface with local and U.S. government authorities.

description:

Location: Livingston

Salary: £25,000 p/a

Benefits: Private Healthcare, Pension, 25 days holiday rising to 30 over 5 years, Group Life Insurance, Income Protection, Gym Discounts, Employee of the Quarter, Employee Referral program and many more.

Passionate about technology and helping people? As an L1 Service Desk Analyst in Livingston, where you'll be the first point of contact for customers, resolving technical issues and ensuring a seamless support experience from start to finish/

- Strong customer service skills with a customer-first approach
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills
- Experience using ticketing or call-tracking systems
- Ability to prioritise and manage multiple tasks effectively
- Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills
- A proactive attitude and willingness to take ownership of issues
